<reason>CON won a close, high-quality clash by making the net comparison easier to decide: a visible late bargain is mostly a transfer plus extra labor and a thinner 5 p.m. market, so the proposing side never showed the duty beats those costs. PRO was coherent on sunk costs, bounded opportunity, and buyer surplus, and forced CON to concede the markdown itself is a transfer, but did not close the net-benefit or enforcement gap. CON’s dumpster-price alternative also answered the methane point without conscripting the aisle.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s reply to the transfer question: once shopper savings are counted, the remaining loss is handling, waiting, and the missing regular chicken—then using earlier culls to show PRO’s records cannot catch the rational evasion path.</best_rebuttal>
